pageQuotes.excerpt: Z Fellows | Get Fast-Tracked into Silicon Valley Z Fellows About Mentors FAQs Blog Startup Workshop Apply Now 1 week. $10,000. Your Fast-Track Into Silicon Valley. A one-week experience bringing you together with founders of multi billion dollar companies. Apply Now There's a pattern among the most successful founders. They all started by learning from those who have built multi billion dollar companies. Getting mentored by proven founders is the fastest way to accelerate. Success leaves clues—follow them. Sergey brin & Larry Page (Founders of google) Mentored by Andy Bechtolsheim (founder of Sun Microsystems) mark zuckerberg (Founder of Facebook) Mentored by Peter Thiel (founder of PayPal) Steve Chen, Chad Hurley & Jawed Karim (Founders of YouTube) Mentored by Roelof Botha (PayPal CFO & Sequoia Capital) Z Fellows connects really early builders with multi billion dollar founders. Who are Z Fellows? Z Fellows are technical builders of all ages working on side projects and startups. We are your first believer . We’ve worked with high school dropouts, college students, and people with full-time jobs across a variety of industries including consumer, social, enterprise, defense, healthcare, edtech, fintech, gaming, cloud infrastructure, cybersecurity, crypto, AI, ML, climate, biotech, and more. Realize this, and you will find strength.” “The happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.” “If you are distressed by anything external, the pain is not due to the thing itself, but to your estimate of it; and this you have the power to revoke at any moment.” “It is not death that a man should fear, but he should fear never beginning to live.” “Don't go on discussing what a good person should be. Just be one.” Source: Meditations by Marcus Aurelius 2: Elon Musk’s algorithm for managing companies Question every requirement — “Each should come with the name of the person who made it. Requirements from smart people are the most dangerous, because people are less likely to question them. Always do so, even if the requirement came from me. Then make the requirements less dumb.“ Delete any part or process you can — “You may have to add them back later. In fact, if you do not end up adding back at least 10% of them, then you didn’t delete enough.“ Simplify and optimize — “A common mistake is to simplify and optimize a part or a process that should not exist.” Accelerate cycle time —
